title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
hints: insert and remove need to be fast - a hash map from value to its index in a backing array, combined with swap-and-pop removal, gets you both in O(1) average
for remove, instead of shifting elements after deleting, swap the target with the last element in the array, then pop the last element - update the hash map for the swapped value's new index

getRandom here always wants the smallest present value, which a plain array or hash map can't give you in O(1) - what structure keeps fast access to the minimum while still supporting removal of an arbitrary value?

a min-heap gives fast access to the minimum, but lazily skipping stale entries (or tracking how many times a value has been removed) lets you handle heap entries that no longer belong to the set, or use a balanced ordered structure (like a sorted set / TreeMap) for guaranteed O(log n) insert, remove, and find-min
commonMistakes: forgetting insert must return 0 (and leave the set unchanged) when the value is already present
forgetting remove must return 0 when the value isn't present
using a linear scan for getRandom or for presence checks, which defeats the point of the O(1)/O(log n) target
when swap-and-pop removing from a backing array, forgetting to update the hash map's stored index for the element swapped into the removed slot
treating getRandom's redefinition as literal randomness and using a real RNG, which won't produce checkable, deterministic results here

content.problemStatement:
Design a data structure that supports three operations on a set of
integers, all efficiently: insert a value, remove a value, and fetch a
value currently in the set. You're given a space-delimited sequence of
operations to run starting from an empty set. Each token is one of:

- `insert_<value>` - insert value if it isn't already present
- `remove_<value>` - remove value if it is present
- `getRandom` - report an element currently in the set

**Simulate the operations in order and return a list containing the
result of every insert, remove, and getRandom call, in that order.**

Since a real random pick can't be checked deterministically, this
version redefines getRandom to always report the smallest value
currently present in the set, so results are checkable. Insert and
remove are expected to run in O(1) average time via a hash map, while
this deterministic getRandom naturally costs O(log n) using an ordered
structure such as a min-heap or a balanced/sorted set.

- `insert` returns 1 if the value was newly added, or 0 if it was already present
- `remove` returns 1 if the value was present and removed, or 0 if it wasn't present
- `getRandom` is never called on an empty set
constraints: tokens are separated by single spaces, and insert/remove tokens join the operation and value with an underscore
values fit in a standard 32-bit integer and may be negative
getRandom is never called while the set is empty
notes: inserting the same value twice in a row
removing a value that was never inserted
removing a value, then re-inserting it later
getRandom called when the set has exactly one element

sampleTestCases.input: ops = "insert_1 insert_2 insert_2 getRandom remove_1 getRandom"
sampleTestCases.explanation: insert 1 (new, 1); insert 2 (new, 1); insert 2 again (already present, 0); getRandom reports smallest present = 1; remove 1 (present, 1); getRandom reports smallest present = 2
insert 5 (new, 1); remove 5 (present, 1); remove 5 again (not present anymore, 0)
all three inserts are new; the set is {1,2,3} and getRandom reports the smallest, 1

optimal.time: O(1) average for insert/remove, O(log n) for getRandom
optimal.pattern: hash map (value -> index) with swap-and-pop array removal for O(1) insert/remove, plus a min-heap or ordered set to answer getRandom in O(log n)

bruteForce.approach: keep the elements in a plain list; insert appends only if not already present (checked via a linear scan), remove does a linear scan to find and delete the value, and getRandom scans the whole list for the minimum every time
